1.why: Every screen is a static, single-column card layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs anywhere in the ten steps.

2.why: Bold dark headings, coloured callout bars and a single solid blue primary button make the key action stand out, though the repeated 'Keep your account safe' block and the large black log panel compete for attention.

3.why: Each step has only one main field and button, but the needed item is surrounded by repeated safety boilerplate and a technical 'Recovery activity logs' console that adds visual searching.

4.why: Rules are shown on-screen when needed (password criteria list, demo MFA code 246810 displayed, token pre-filled), so little must be held in memory, although it is still a 10-step sequence.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the new-password step.

6.why: Apart from the recovery token being pre-populated in step 3, nothing familiar is surfaced — no masked email echo, no saved account, no device recognition.

7.why: Sentences are short and legibly sized, but wording includes technical terms such as 'recovery token', 'MFA code' and 'No more than 72 UTF-8 bytes (bcrypt limit)', plus raw log text.

8.why: No error or validation state is shown in any of the ten screenshots, so the claim that error messages explain the problem and the fix cannot be observed to hold.

9.why: The demo code (246810) and pre-filled token effectively show what to enter, but there are no input placeholders or example formats for the email or the new password.

10.why: Only a single password-plus-code path exists; no choice of authentication method (code, biometric/face, passkey) is offered or explained anywhere.

11.why: Each screen presents essentially one decision and one primary button, with at most a single secondary option such as 'Start over'.

12.why: Each action produces an explicit confirmation banner and a timestamped log entry, ending with 'Recovery complete – Your password has been updated and the privacy statement acknowledgement has been recorded.'

13.why: Every step carries a short guidance callout (e.g. 'recovery tokens expire quickly and can be used once') plus visible password rules and safety tips.

14.why: 'Start over' (step 2) and 'Begin another recovery' (step 10) allow restarting, but intermediate steps have no back link, no 'resend code' and no way to correct an earlier entry without restarting.

15.why: Header, card styling, callout bars, button colours and the log panel are identical across all ten steps, giving a highly predictable, learnable layout.
